TSN Talks S2 E6: Sakol Sachdev, Founder & CEO of Micro Greentech

What if the things we throw away every day — used cooking oil, food scraps, plastic bottles — could power planes, feed soil, and earn people money?
  
That's not a future scenario. That's what Mr. Sakol Sachdev is building right now. He's the first Thai-Indian entrepreneur to pitch on Thailand's Shark Tank — and get on offer for $1M USD. But that was just the beginning. Did he eventually receive it? Sakol reveals it all in this TSN Talks Episode.

Sakol built his empire from scratch, fighting for legality before the law even existed, patenting what no one else dared to, and building an ecosystem that today runs 500+ stations, with over 1M litres sold a year and tens of thousands of machines serving several communities in Thailand.

  In this episode, we go deep:

  → The Shark Tank story — what really happened, and what came after
  → Patent Strategy every innovator needs to hear
  → His 5 innovations that could change Thailand's future:
    — Smart gas cylinder exchange
    — Plastic waste reverse vending machines
    — Used cooking oil converted to jet fuel
    — Food waste turned to fertilizer in 24 hours
    — A carbon credit platform backed by the UN Global Compact
  → Why Sakol is learning AI at 50 — and why he says you have no choice
  → The best free lesson in entrepreneurship he ever got
  → His take on oil prices, gold, crypto, and why saving is not a strategy

TSN Talks S2 E9, Mr. Deepak Sajnani, President of Thai-Sindhi Association

Next up on TSN Talks, we have the honor of hosting a respected business leader, former Director of the India-Thai Chamber of Commerce (ITCC) and current President of the Thai Sindhi Association, Mr. Deepak Sajnani.

Mr Deepak Sajnani takes us through his journey from arriving in Bangkok as an 18-year-old to building four shops by the age of 23, and eventually running businesses across bespoke tailoring, real estate, jewellery and retail. He has spent decades not only building businesses, but contributing to the wider Indian community in Thailand.

We talk about the lessons he learned along the way, from meeting the third richest man in Denmark and learning how to sell, to building seven businesses, investing in Med Park Hospital, and finding the right balance between ambition and giving back.

He also shares four rules he'd give to any young person starting out, including a philosophy that has guided him throughout his life:

TSN Talks Ep. 14 - Mahima Natarajan, Co-Founder & CMO of Yindii

🔥 What does it take to turn food waste into one of Asia’s hottest startups?

In this episode of TSN Talks, we sit down with Mahima Rajangam Natarajan, Co-Founder & CMO of Yindii. What began as a simple WordPress site and one supermarket partner has become a regional movement: 700,000+ downloads, 1,500+ brand partners, 500,000 meals saved, and 3 countries impacted.

Mahima’s journey is one of grit, purpose, and vision. After years working in the corporate world, she decided to take on one of the biggest environmental challenges of our time: food waste. What began as a simple WordPress site and a single partner merchant in Sukhumvit has grown into a movement with over 700,000 app downloads, 1,500+ brand partners, and operations across 3 countries. Together, the Yindii community has saved more than half a million meals and offset 1,250 tons of CO₂, proving that sustainability and scale can go hand in hand.

On TSN Talks, Mahima takes us inside the journey: from early struggles and unexpected breakthroughs to building a movement of “food heroes” and proving that startups can drive real climate impact.

If you’ve ever wondered how purpose and business can collide to create lasting change, this episode is for you.

TSN Talks S2 E8: Angad Pasricha, Founder of Human Stories Thailand

Why are we more connected than ever… yet lonelier than ever?

That question led Angad Pasricha to build Human Stories Thailand—a community designed to help strangers become genuine friends through storytelling, vulnerability, and shared experiences.

But Human Stories didn't begin in Bangkok.

In this episode of TSN Talks, Angad shares how a single event in New York changed the way he thinks about connection, why he chose to pursue an MBA in Columbia University, how he exited an EdTech startup serving hundreds of thousands of students, and why he believes modern networking has become too transactional.

We also explore why vulnerability feels uncomfortable in Asian cultures, what it really takes to build meaningful communities, and whether AI will bring us closer together—or further apart.

What we cover:

→ The New York experience that inspired Human Stories Thailand
→ Why he left banking to pursue an MBA in New York
→ Building and scaling an EdTech startup with his sister
→ Growing to 250,000+ students and 700,000+ transactions
→ Why people feel lonelier than ever in 2026
→ Creating spaces where strangers feel safe to open up
→ Building community in a "save face" culture
→ The future of human connection in an AI-first world

"Society doesn't really exist. You yourself are society."

TSN Talks Ep 20: Harprem Doowa, Founder & CEO of Eazy Digital

🚨 This week on TSN Talks… we sit down with Harprem Doowa — the entrepreneur behind PetLoft, Frank.co, and now Eazy Digital.

In this episode, we talk about his journey from employee to founder, early failures, building Frank from the ground up, navigating a major exit, and starting again with Eazy Digital. Harprem breaks down the real reality of building products inside Thailand’s startup ecosystem.

From graduating and taking his first job, to pursuing an MBA at Sasin, to launching PetLoft as his first step into entrepreneurship — Harprem shares how each chapter shaped his mindset. We also dive into the his journey and rise with Frank.co, one of Southeast Asia’s first digital insurance platforms, how it scaled, and what came after the big exit.

TSN Talks S2:E5: Gagan Ajmani | Thai Founders Think Too Small? Hear from the Guy Who Raised $120M

From ₹0 savings to managing $40M in VC funds, then building a startup that raised $120M across 3 countries. Gagan's journey from India to Bangkok is one of the most honest entrepreneurship stories we've heard on TSN Talks.

He built Delivery (now Transportify), got sued in the Philippines, navigated a market crash and came out the other side with WOWS Global, a private market platform helping founders and SMEs in Thailand access capital and fractional CFO support.

This episode is for anyone building something, doubting themselves, or trying to figure out how to think bigger.

TSN Talks S2 E4: Sukhdev Sethi |  He Closed $1.5M and Beat 6,000 People from 151 Countries in Sales.

Sukhdev Sethi (Dev Sethi), Global Sales Champion & Business Coach. 

In this episode of TSN Talks, we sit down with Sukhdev Sethi, a man who went from being an IT programmer to a global sales champion, beating over 6,000 competitors across 151 countries and closing $1.5 million in sales.

But this isn't your typical success story. 

He quit a dream corporate job that gave him a brand new car every 11 months. He launched his business in December 2019, and then COVID shut down the world. He worked 90 hours a week for 18 months straight without a single day off.
How did he come out on top? One skill: sales.

Sukhdev shares his Premium Client System (Position, Offer, Close), the concept of skill stacking, and the 5 skills that AI can never replace, skills that might be the most important thing you learn this year. 

As of 2026, he has helped his clients close over $10M AUD in Sales. 

Whether you're an entrepreneur, a freelancer, or someone stuck in a 9-to-5 wondering "what's next" — this is the conversation that could change everything.
